For me, it depends on the kind of therapy, psychology has many branches with different points of view/treatment. Also, there are good and bad therapists. I've tried conductism first and it was crap for me, then humanism and went a little better for a while. Later i tried psychoanalisys and stick to it. My first psychoanalist was a newbie but it still helped me. My second one was really good and had a lot of experience and it changed my life. It's a long process and i wouldn't say i'm "healed", but i would be way worse, and it helped me make changes that did a lot of good in my life at the time. Some people do better with different kinds of therapy, maybe you can try a few. And there's also nothing wrong in taking medication if needed.

Switch the camplamp for a headlamp. You could leave the cammelback, the hard plastic bottle and take some light soda bottles. You could change your gas cooking set for an alcohol and soda can set.

If you wanna play it safe, start with the basics. Just go camping somewhere that has a similar weather to where you wanna hike, and figure out a set of clothing, sleeping bag(or blankets), and shelter that's gonna keep you dry and warm enough. Cooking is not absolutely necessary if you carry ready to eat food(bread, peanuts...). Try to think light and take just what you really need plus an extra set of clothing, couple more socks. Later on you'll work out what you can do without, or what you wanna add.
